decisive_items: clonal amplification product for the γ-chain of the T-cell receptor
small to medium-sized, atypical lymphocytes with focal areas of epidermotropism
No atypical cells were found in the peripheral blood
response.rationale: The clonal T-cell receptor amplification, atypical epidermotropic lymphocytes, and absence of circulating atypical cells fit mycosis fungoides specifically, whereas Sézary syndrome requires Sézary cells in blood. Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma is broader and less precise.

rejected.why: No atypical cells in peripheral blood contradicts Sézary syndrome, which requires circulating atypical lymphocytes.
Less specific than mycosis fungoides; the findings are classic for mycosis fungoides, a subtype of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma.
